Here, the factor of 2 in (1.3) is to force p +2 η to be odd; provided of course p = 2. Combining Theorems 1.2 and 1.3, we have that every large N ≥ 1 can be represented as the sum of a prime and a number with at most 3 prime factors. Any further lowering of the number of prime factors in Chen or Li's results appears out of reach, so we do not attempt this here.
